target_customer: Decision makers in markets and macro, deals and legal events, policy and regulation, and business planning who pay for calibrated forecasts of global events
problem: Decision makers need calibrated probabilities on open geopolitical, economic and legal questions, and human forecasting is slow and hard to scale. Preseen builds AI forecasting agents that publish a median and an 80 percent range for each question.
business_model: Forecast subscriptions and sales-led access (book a call or waitlist); pricing not public
product_category: AI forecasting agents for global macro events

founders.name: Veniamin Veselovsky
prior_employers: Ukrainian startup building interactive tables (brief stint)
education: Princeton PhD student working on large language models (completion not stated on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he also did research in Toronto, Switzerland and Germany. The SPC post says he built the data layer: crawlers and normalization pipelines over country APIs, satellite imagery and procurement records.

founders.name: Theodore Summer
founders.background_notes: SPC post says he built a GPT-4 forecasting tool in 2022 and discarded it, rebuilt it in 2025, won a Metaculus tournament and quit a software job. A wire story reports he turned $35 into about $1.9 million on Kalshi over seven months. Employer not named.

competitors.name: Mantic
competitors.what: London AI startup forecasting world events, won prize money in the Q1 2025 Metaculus AI benchmark
competitors.traction_then: emerged from stealth in August 2025 with a Metaculus benchmark result

technical_complexity.rationale: Calibrated LLM forecasting agents need heterogeneous data ingestion (country APIs, satellite imagery, procurement records) and benchmark-grade accuracy, which Metaculus tournaments publicly test.

defensibility.rationale: Public track records and a data pipeline help, but forecasting agents can be rebuilt by well-funded labs and rivals such as Mantic.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge as of late 2026; a funded UK rival and prediction markets occupy the space.

market_need_then: Prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket were growing in 2025 and AI bots were competing in Metaculus tournaments, showing interest in machine forecasts. Paying demand for macro forecasts was not documented in sources found.

branding.domain_note: Uses preseen.com, the exact name; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Simple wordmark in dark and light versions
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, concise, forward-looking; taglines such as See the future before it arrives

branding.brand_signature: Public forecast track record, including first place among bots in the Metaculus Cup Spring 2026 per its site
branding.community_and_virality: Founder Kalshi story was syndicated in wire coverage in October 2026; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Early brand with a credible accuracy narrative and some press via the founder story, but little independent brand coverage.

outcome_analysis: Preseen is active and young. The YC S25 company raised a seed round led by South Park Commons in July 2026 and claims strong public forecasting results, which supported fundraising. Amount is undisclosed in the sources opened, and no shutdown, acquisition or layoff was found. The main risks are well-funded rivals and unproven willingness to pay.
notes: Caplight lists total funding of $5.6M and an 11 person team; seen only on an aggregator snippet, so unverified and not recorded as a round amount. YC lists team size 1. The YC page also features a launch for a different product named Rid with a different cofounder; not treated as Preseen. Competitor Mantic is dated to the batch period (August 2025).
